overview.description: Bura is a Russian point-trick card game for 2 players that uses a 36-card deck (6 through Ace). Each player receives 3 cards and draws after each trick. The trump suit is set by the last card dealt to the non-dealer. A dramatic feature: once a player believes they have 31 or more points in hand while the stock is exhausted, they may declare 'Bura!' and those trick points are counted immediately. The target is 31 points.

history.origins: A traditional Russian 2-player card game of the point-trick family. Bura is closely related to other Eastern European draw-trump games. Documented in Russian card game literature through the 20th century.
timeline: 1900s: Standard across Russia and Soviet Union households.
Present: Still played in Russia; digital versions exist.
history.evolution: The 'Bura!' declaration mechanic gives the game an exciting tensionâ€”players race to accumulate 31 points while managing the declaration risk.
history.cultural: A beloved Russian domestic game, often played by two people without any additional equipment.

setup.dealing: Deal 3 cards each. Turn the last card face-up as trump indicator; place it under the stock pile with the suit visible.

rules.objective: Accumulate 31 or more card points in your trick pile.
rules.gameplay: Lead any card. No follow-suit obligation. Highest trump wins; else highest led-suit card. Winner draws first, loser draws second. Winner leads next. Continue until stock exhausted.
keyRules: Trump (set by last dealt card) beats any off-suit.
After stock exhausted, must follow suit.
'Bura!' can be declared only after stock is empty.

strategy.basic: Protect Aces and Tensâ€”they are your primary point sources (11 and 10 pts each).
strategy.intermediate: Track your running point total. Know when to push for the final trick vs. let the opponent win junk. The Bura declaration is a commitmentâ€”miscounting is fatal.
strategy.advanced: Trump Management: Save trump for high-point captures (opponent's Ace or Ten). No follow-suit makes it dangerous to lead Aces into potential enemy trump traps.
tips: An Ace + Ten = 21 points. Win both and you're 2/3 of the way to Bura.
Once stock is empty, follow-suit is mandatoryâ€”plan your endgame carefully.

trumpConfig.trumpSuitRanking: Standard A-high in trump; trump beats any off-suit.
trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Higher card of same suit or any trump beats a card.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: May lead 1, 2, or 3 cards of the same suit.

edgeCases.text: Bura declaration allowed only after stock is exhausted; claim must be from memory without looking at tricks.
False claim (30 or fewer points) doubles the pot; claimer still deals next hand.
No requirement to follow suit while stock remains; after stock is empty play continues from hand.
Special combinations can steal the lead: Bura (three trumps) wins the pot immediately; three aces and Molodka (three same plain suit) let that player lead the next trick.
If not enough cards in stock to refill everyone to 3, remaining stock is not used; players continue with cards in hand.
Winner of each trick draws first from stock, then others in clockwise order, until each has three cards again.

customActions.description: Dealer gives 3 cards to each player one at a time, turns the next card face up for trump, and places the rest of the deck face down on top of it so the trump suit remains visible.
customActions.constraints: Dealer only; performed once at start of hand.

customActions.description: Lead one card or two or three cards of the same suit. Others play the same number of cards; no requirement to follow suit. A card is beaten by a higher card of the same suit or by any trump; to beat a multi-card lead, beat each card individually.
customActions.constraints: When leading, must lead 1–3 cards of same suit. When following, play same number of cards as led; any cards allowed.

customActions.description: Claim to have 31 or more card points in your tricks. Claim must be from memory; players may not look at their tricks. If correct, you win the pot; if wrong (30 or fewer), you double the pot. Claimer deals the next hand.
customActions.constraints: Only when stock is exhausted. Claim ends the play immediately.

engine.deckDescription: One standard 36-card deck: nine ranks (six through ace) in each of four suits. No jokers; used for Bura (Russian card game) where the goal is to take tricks and score points with aces, kings, and other point cards.
engine.suitDescription: Four suits (typically French: spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs). Trump is determined by the last card dealt or by the dealer's choice; follow suit when able. Standard 36-card trick and point order apply.
engine.rankDescription: Nine ranks per suit: six, seven, eight, nine, ten, jack, queen, king, ace. In trump the order may differ (jack and nine often high). Point values: ace 11, ten 10, king 4, queen 3, jack 2; others zero.

synthesis.shortDescription: Russia's fast 2-player point-trick game. Play freely for tricks until the stock runs dryâ€”then follow suit strictly and race to 31 card points. Declare 'Bura!' when you're sure you've hit the target.

prompts.human: You've won the Ace of Spades (11), Ten of Hearts (10), and King of Clubs (4) = 25 points. Two tricks remain. Even winning just one more trick with a Queen (3pts) = 28â€”not enough. You need 6 more points. Win one more trick with a Ten or Ace, or two tricks with face cards.
